articles.title: Three Booleans Is Not a State Machine: Modelling UI Logic That Can't Be in Two States at Once
articles.excerpt: I review a lot of component code. The most common bug pattern I see is not a typo. It is this: const [isLoading, setIsLoading] = useState(false); const [isError, setIsError] = useState(false); const […
articles.body: I review a lot of component code. The most common bug pattern I see is not a typo. It is this: const [ isLoading , setIsLoading ] = useState ( false ) ; const [ isError , setIsError ] = useState ( false ) ; const [ isSuccess , setIsSuccess ] = useState ( false ) ; Three booleans, eight combinations, three of which are legal. The other five are bugs waiting for a slow network. Why the bug is structural, not careless Everyone knows not to set isLoading and isSuccess at the same time. Nobody sets them deliberately. They happen because the flags are set in different places, on different async paths, sometimes in an await that resolves after the component re-rendered. Add a quantity and a retryCount and the handshake gets worse.

articles.title: SecurityException Kills HDMI-CEC Power Control on Sideloads
articles.excerpt: Conclusion Android's HdmiControlManager exposes HDMI-CEC control APIs (standby, wakeup, etc.) that require signature|privileged permission, so calling them from a sideloaded app throws SecurityExcepti…
articles.body: Conclusion Android's HdmiControlManager exposes HDMI-CEC control APIs (standby, wakeup, etc.) that require signature|privileged permission, so calling them from a sideloaded app throws SecurityException on most devices, making the call an effective no-op. A fleet of signage devices (Google TVs locked down as Device Owner kiosks) wanted to turn the screen fully off at night via a genuine HDMI-CEC standby, but this constraint forced the real mechanism away from CEC and onto DevicePolicyManager.lockNow() instead. Symptom The signage devices are Google TVs mounted as hallway displays, locked into kiosk mode via Device Owner, with the screen meant to turn off at night and back on in the morning. The first approach considered was dropping the TV itself into a genuine HDMI-CEC standby.

articles.title: An inference speedup has to beat its own error bar
articles.excerpt: Every local-inference thread I have read this year ends with someone claiming a percentage. Nobody shows the spread, and half of those claims are measuring noise, that is what an afternoon of tuning o…
articles.body: Every local-inference thread I have read this year ends with someone claiming a percentage. Nobody shows the spread, and half of those claims are measuring noise, that is what an afternoon of tuning on my own hardware proved. A tuning win needs four things before the number means anything: a median, an error bar wide enough to see, proof the changed flag actually loaded into the running process, and a stability gate where a crash at load is a discard. I got all four working on a live coding lane of my dual-3090 Arch box on November 17, 2026, and shipped nothing to production. The ledger came back empty of wins, and that empty result is more useful than a 3% headline would have been.

articles.body: Implementing a welcome email feature using email APIs in a healthtech marketplace starts with a constraint: where seller and order data may travel. The Node.js application needs to welcome a seller and, later, notify that seller about a new order. A convenient email client becomes expensive to integrate if the team discovers afterward that its message bodies, delivery records, or support logs cross an unapproved processor boundary. TL;DR: For a Node.js welcome email feature, separate application events, template management, and delivery adapters. Prefer a unified API when its processing arrangement passes the same region, retention, and deletion review as a direct provider. Choose a direct specialist when the approval depends on that provider's specific contractual boundary.

ReportURI said it identified 178 websites—including CNN, Zoom, the BBC, and Salesforce—that were affected. JavaScript digitally signed by Optimizely and then loaded into customer pages had been modified to include malicious components that attempted to infect visitor devices with multiple payloads. When wares were installed successfully, they swapped user cryptocurrency wallet addresses for the attackers.

articles.title: NASA's Voyager 1 launched second, so how did it beat Voyager 2 to a light-day by nearly a decade?
articles.excerpt: Voyager 1 just reached a light-day in space, but Voyager 2 won't do the same until 2035, due to speed choices made throughout their 50-year missions.
articles.body: Voyager 1 is about to reach a light-day of distance in space, but Voyager 2 won't hit the mark until about 2035. Why the big difference? On Nov. 18, Voyager 1 will be so far away from Earth that it will take a full light-day (24 hours) to send a signal to the distant spacecraft, at 16,094,799,096 miles (25,902,068,356 kilometers). Since light is essentially the maximum speed in the universe (absent using devices like wormholes, or quantum-physics puzzles), it's a big deal — so big that NASA will be celebrating the milestone by asking fans to shine Morse Code signals at the sky. But why will Voyager 2 take nearly a decade longer?

articles.excerpt: The British company Foundational thinks its laser-reflecting tech can help humanity fight the space-junk problem — and it just proved out a demo version in an orbital test.
articles.body: A British startup thinks it can help humanity deal with its space junk problem. Millions of pieces of space debris circle Earth at the moment, according to the European Space Agency (ESA). Even the smallest fragments are potentially dangerous, given how fast stuff travels in orbit. Experts have proposed a range of measures to deal with this junk. The smallest bits, for example, may require big space nets, or lasering the stuff down to Earth. Large satellites are increasingly being deliberately deorbited these days, and a few have even been refueled to keep them operating in orbit — something that will likely start happening more and more over the coming years. Now, the British startup Foundational has another idea to throw into the mix: retroreflectors.

articles.body: 4 Min Read New Album of Baby Star Sounds Shared by NASA’s Chandra A new album from NASA’s Chandra X-ray Observatory collects snapshots of baby stars across the galaxy and beyond and transforms that data into sound. Four new sonifications use data of stars that are actively forming, captured by Chandra and other NASA telescopes By studying places in the universe where stars are currently being born and young stars are present, astronomers can better understand the lifecycle of all stars, including our own Sun. articles.title: 'Neuromancer:' Release date, cast & everything we know about Apple TV's new cyberpunk series
articles.excerpt: Hack into our handy guide to this electrifying adaptation of William Gibson’s cult ‘80s novel.
articles.body: We're in a bit of a cyberpunk revival at the moment. 2026 gave the excellent second season of Netflix’s "Cyberpunk: Edgerunners," and Prime Video's " Blade Runner 2099 " is just around the corner. 2027 will continue this trend with " Neuromancer " blasting onto Apple TV. Based on cyberspace guru William Gibson’s seminal 1984 novel, "Neuromancer" follows Case, a brilliant hacker who falls into a web of digital espionage and crime as he attempts an impossible corporate heist. The pulp noir novel has been hailed as a generational revelation, and its slang and terminology have become ingrained in computer nerd subcultures.
